questions.question:
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘÷’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged?

8 + 6 ÷ 51 – 17 × 13 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/952c967501c582f1911db7fefdaaefa9b6e3f505512624eb925e04e002be5a1f.png] 

Given equation: 8 + 6 ÷ 51 – 17 × 13 = ?

According to the question, after ‘÷’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged:

8 + 6 ÷ 51 – 17 × 13 = ? ⇒ 8 × 6 - 51 ÷ 17 + 13 = ?

⇒ 8 × 6 - __51 ____÷____ 17__ + 13 = ?

⇒ __8 ×____ 6__ - 3 + 13 = ?

⇒ __48 + 13__ - 3 = ?

⇒ __6____1 - ____3__ = ?

⇒ 58 = ?

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the triad in which the numbers are related to each other in the same way as the numbers in the following triads.

8-17-35

23-47-95

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to

be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given

statements.

Statements:

All apples are mangoes.

All mangoes are lemons.

All lemons are kiwis.

Conclusions:

(I) All apples are lemons.

(II) All mangoes are kiwis.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0bce150fb31753928f0b960570cd0eb1553bec7197c53e6fd8ff41d89d66c470.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) All apples are lemons → Follow (As all apples are mangoes and all mangoes are lemons. As wholes apples comes in mangoes which whole comes in lemons, therefore it is true.)

(II) All mangoes are kiwis → Follow (As all mangoes are lemons and all lemons are kiwis. As wholes mangoes comes in lemons which whole comes in kiwis, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Both conclusions I and II follow.

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Option 1) 90 – 144

__90 × 1.6__ = 144

144 = 144 (LHS = RHS)

Option 2) 75 – 120

__75 × 1.6__ = 120

120 = 120 (LHS = RHS)

Option 3) 45 – 70

__45 × 1.6__ = 70

**72 ≠ 70 (LHS ≠ RHS)**

Option 4) 65 – 104

__65 × 1.6__ = 104

104 = 104 (LHS = RHS)

Thus, out of all the options, '45 – 70' is the odd one out.

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true,

even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s

from the given statements.

Statements:

All pens are pages.

Some pages are pins.

Some pins are boards.

Conclusions:

(I) Some pins are pens.

(II) Some boards are pages.

(III) Some pens are boards.

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3cb3522a5f89ca5206ff50e480624d8996b1a28aac9263762ad4deba2fc46c64.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some pins are pens→ **Does not** follow (As all pens are pages and some pages are pins. So it is possible but not definite.)

(II) Some boards are pages → Does not follow (As some pages are pins and some pins are boards. So it is possible but not definite.)

(III) Some pens are boards → Does not follow (As all pens are pages, some pages are pins and some pins are boards. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, None of the conclusions follow.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
‘Lavish’ is related to ‘Austere’ in the same way as ‘Prejudiced’ is related to ‘________’.

(The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of

letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

‘**Lavish**’ is antonym of ‘**Austere**’.

Similarly,

‘**Prejudiced**’ is antonym of ‘**Impartial**'.

Hence, **"Option 1"** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**Lavish → It means luxurious or extravagant.

Austere → It means simple or strict.

Prejudiced → It means showing partiality or bias.

Impartial → It means fair or unbiased.

Compromised → It means exposed to risk or weakened or to settle a dispute by mutual concessions.

Thoughtful → It means showing consideration or careful thinking.

Careful → It means taking precautions to avoid harm, error, or risk.

questions.question:
Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete

the letter series.

_ C _ W _ _ _ C _ W _ _
questions.solution:
Given series: _ C _ W _ _ _ C _ W _ _

Option 1) WCCWWWCC→ __W__ C __C__ W __C__ __W__ __W__ C __W__ W __C__ __C__ → (It doesn't follow any pattern)

Option 2) WWCWWWCW → __**W**__ C __**W**__ W __**C**__ __**W**__ __**W**__ C __**W**__ W __**C**__ __**W**__ → (It follows the pattern of: WCW - WCW - WCW - WCW)

Option 3) CWCWWCCW → __C__ C __W__ W __C__ __W__ __W__ C __C__ W __C__ __W__ → (It doesn't follow any pattern)

Option 4) CCWWCCWC → __C__ C __C__ W __W__ __W__ __C__ C __C__ W __W__ **__C__** → (It doesn't follow any pattern)

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.
